description: Monophonic synth voice with a drum machine and an eight-step sequencer, after the Korg monotribe: one oscillator through a filter and an envelope, three drum parts, a ribbon strip and a delay

params.text: Picks one of the six octaves marked 64' down to 2'
Sets the level of the synth voice, and at its bottom stop it also switches the filter and the LFO off
Picks the oscillator's waveform, square, triangle or sawtooth
Sets the level of the three drum parts, and at zero the bass drum, snare and hi-hat jacks are silent
Drives the synth voice into a distortion, and at zero a gentler soft clipper takes its place
Sets the delay time, 10ms at the bottom of its travel and 2 seconds at the top
Sets how much of the delayed signal is mixed in, and at zero the delay is out of the path altogether
Selects the snare, so the eight step buttons switch its hits on and off
Switches flux mode, in which recording writes what you play where it falls rather than snapping it to a step
Starts and stops recording; pressed while the play button is held it starts the sequencer as well
Sets the filter's cutoff, closed at the bottom of its travel and open at the top
Sets the LFO's speed: 0.05Hz to 18Hz in the slow and one-shot modes, 1Hz to 5000Hz in the fast one
Sets how far the LFO moves whatever it is aimed at, ten times the reading on the knob
Mixes noise in with the oscillator before the filter, white or pink according to the menu
Sets the filter's resonance
Picks how far the ribbon strip reaches: KEY gives twelve semitones, NARROW two octaves, WIDE five
Picks the envelope: ATTACK gives a soft attack and release, GATE follows the gate squarely, DECAY plucks and falls away
Aims the LFO at the filter, at the oscillator, or at both with half as much going to the oscillator
Picks the LFO's range: 1SHOT runs one slow cycle for each new note, SLOW is the same range free running, FAST reaches audio rates
Picks the LFO's waveform, square, triangle or sawtooth
Sets the sequencer's tempo, 10 to 600 beats a minute unless the menu has narrowed the range
Selects the synth part, so the eight step buttons mute and unmute its steps
Selects the bass drum, so the eight step buttons switch its hits on and off
Selects the hi-hat, so the eight step buttons switch its hits on and off
Held down, it turns the eight step buttons into skip switches: a step switched off is passed over instead of being silent
Switches this step of the selected part on or off; held with the active-step button it skips the step instead, and ctrl-clicking it cycles that step through accent, glide, both and neither
Starts and stops the sequencer
Held down, it hands the ribbon strip over to gate length, or to a drum roll when a drum part is selected, instead of to pitch
Sets how much an accented step lifts the filter's cutoff and how far a gliding step slides

inputs.text: Pitch for the oscillator, one volt per octave, added to the octave knob
A voltage above 1V opens the envelope and sounds the oscillator
Audio mixed in ahead of the filter at one and a half times its own level; anything above 0.1V here also fires the envelope
A rising edge past 1V moves the sequencer on a step, and while a cable is here the tempo knob is hidden
Sets the octave outright, -5V to 5V across the six positions, and the knob is moved to match
Sets the cutoff outright, -5V to 5V across the whole knob, and the knob is moved to match
Sets the resonance outright, -5V to 5V across the whole knob, and the knob is moved to match
Sets the level outright, -5V to 5V across the whole knob, and the knob is moved to match
Sets the LFO frequency outright in hertz, -5V to 5V giving 0Hz to 1Hz, and while a cable is here the rate knob and the mode switch are hidden
Sets the LFO depth outright, -5V to 5V across the whole knob, and the knob is moved to match
Sets the distortion outright, -5V to 5V across the whole knob, and the knob is moved to match
A rising edge past 1V sets the delay time from the gap between edges, anything from 10ms to 4 seconds, and while a cable is here the delay time knob is hidden
Sets the delay mix outright, -5V to 5V across the whole knob, and the knob is moved to match
Sets the noise level outright, -5V to 5V across the whole knob, and the knob is moved to match
Sets the accent and glide amount outright, -5V to 5V across the whole knob, and the knob is moved to match

outputs.text: The pitch the voice is playing, one volt per octave
The gate the voice is playing
Everything the module makes, the synth voice and the three drums together
A pulse on each sequencer step, sent at 5.01V plus a hundredth of a volt for each step, so a second Clonotribe with Match Steps switched on follows the same step
The synth voice alone, without the drums
The bass drum alone, silent while the rhythm knob is at zero
The snare alone, silent while the rhythm knob is at zero
The hi-hat alone, silent while the rhythm knob is at zero
A 1ms 5V pulse each time the LFO completes a cycle

notes: the ribbon strip along the bottom is a drawing rather than a control, so clicking it cannot open a note of its own. Dragging along it plays a pitch and opens the gate.
with the gate-time button held, dragging the ribbon strip sets gate length instead of pitch, or rolls the drum part that is selected.
the bass drum, snare and hi-hat jacks stay at 0V while the rhythm knob is at its bottom stop, which is where it starts, so the drums are silent until you raise it.
keys work while the mouse is over the panel: space plays and stops, shift records, tab switches flux, F5 to F8 pick the part, F9 is active step, F10 is gate time.
the number keys 1 to 8 work the eight step buttons while the mouse is over the panel, and holding ctrl with one of them cycles that step through accent and glide.
menu: Filter Type: Default (MS-20), Ladder (TB-303), Classic (Moog) — picks which of the three filter models the cutoff and peak controls drive
Drum Kit: Original, TR-808, Latin — picks which set of samples the three drum parts use
Noise Type: White, Pink — picks the noise the noise knob mixes in
Tempo range: 10–600 BPM, 20–300 BPM, 60–180 BPM — sets what the tempo knob's travel covers
Clear All Sequences — empties the synth sequence and all three drum patterns
Clear Synth Sequence — empties the synth sequence and leaves the drum patterns alone
Clear Drum Sequence — empties all three drum patterns and leaves the synth sequence alone
Enable All Active Steps — switches every step of the selected part back on
16-step Mode — runs the sequence over sixteen steps instead of eight, with the eight buttons reaching them in two halves
Match Steps — makes the sync input follow the step number encoded in another Clonotribe's sync output rather than only counting edges
